sections.title: Remedial Actions
Threshold gaps
sections.text:
Reduce any excessive gap at the bottom of the door so smoke control is maintained and the door can still operate freely. Re-hang or realign the leaf, correct hinge drop, and fit a compatible threshold seal or automatic drop seal where the doorset evidence allows it.

Where the gap is excessive because the leaf is undersized, over-trimmed, warped, or the floor has been altered beyond the doorset's tolerance, replace the leaf or complete doorset. Use a tested proprietary threshold solution rather than improvised packers, timber strips, or non-tested sealants.

Fire door automatic drop seals typically accommodate maximum gaps (drops) between 14mm and 15mm. These seals are designed for surface-mounted or rebated installation on fire-rated doors (FD30/60) to close the threshold gap, ensuring compliance with fire and smoke safety standards without requiring high fixed thresholds.  

Specialist drop down seals such as (NOR810 rebated drop seal) is fully fire tested to the British Standards BS476: Part 22 has 20mm maximum drop.

sections.title: Perimeter gaps (head and jambs)
sections.text:
Adjust, re-hang, or replace the door or frame so the gaps at the head and jambs are even and controlled all round. Investigate hinge wear, latch misalignment, frame movement, spread of the opening, or leaf distortion where the perimeter gap is excessive, uneven, or tight.

Any trimming must remain within the manufacturer's certified trim allowances. If compliant perimeter gaps cannot be achieved without compromising the doorset, replace the leaf, frame, or complete doorset.

sections.title: Door leaf warped / bowed / twisted
sections.text:
Where the leaf is bowed, twisted, cupped, swollen, or otherwise distorted so that it will not seal, latch, or sit correctly in the frame, replace the door leaf or complete doorset. Minor adjustment of hinges or closers may assist only where distortion is slight and the doorset evidence is not compromised.

Do not rely on excessive closer force, latch adjustment, or packers to pull a distorted leaf into the frame. Persistent warping indicates a defective or damaged leaf and should be treated as a replacement issue.

sections.title: Door leaf over-trimmed / undersized / missing lippings
sections.text:
Where the leaf has been over-trimmed, the core is exposed, the lippings are missing or loose, or the leaf no longer fills the frame within certified tolerances, replace the leaf or complete doorset. Reinstate any approved lippings only where the manufacturer or test evidence permits that repair method.

Do not build up the edges with non-tested timber, filler, mastic, tape, or improvised sections unless there is specific evidence that the repair is suitable for that doorset.

sections.title: Does the door fit correctly in the frame
sections.text:
Re-hang or realign the door so it sits square in the frame, opens freely, and contacts the stops and seals correctly. Correct any dropped hinges, twisted frames, distorted stops, or loose fixings that prevent the leaf from seating properly.

Only plane or trim the door within the certified trim allowances. If the frame is not plumb, loose, spread, or distorted beyond repair, reset or replace the frame and refit or replace the doorset as necessary.

sections.title: Door binding on floor / threshold / frame
sections.text:
Remove the cause of binding so the door can self-close and latch without sticking. Re-hang the leaf, correct hinge drop, trim only within certified allowances, adjust threshold details, and rectify floor finish build-up, carpet changes, or threshold strips that foul the door.

If binding is caused by swelling, warping, over-thick floor finishes, or frame distortion that cannot be corrected compliantly, replace the affected component or complete doorset.

sections.title: Door leaf dropped / sagging on hinges
sections.text:
Rectify dropped leaves by tightening or replacing hinges, repairing fixing points, correcting hinge positions, and realigning the leaf in the frame. Check for worn hinge knuckles, stripped screw holes, frame weakness, and edge damage to the leaf.

If the hanging edge is damaged beyond repair or the drop has resulted from distortion of the leaf or frame, replace the affected component or the complete doorset.

sections.title: Any damage to the door / Any visual defects on the door
sections.text:
Repair minor surface damage only where the repair method is compatible with the door certification or test evidence. Replace the door leaf where there are holes, cracks, splits, delamination, broken panels, severe warping, failed lippings, damaged edges, exposed core, deep impact damage, or any defect likely to reduce fire or smoke performance.

Remove from service and replace any door leaf that has been severely abused, cut, drilled, routed, burnt, soaked, or structurally weakened.

sections.title: Damage type
sections.text: Add damage to door leaf including cracks, splits, holes, impact damage, gouges, delamination, failed lippings, damaged facings, exposed core, warping, moisture damage, rot, burn damage, corrosion to steel skins, or unauthorised alterations.

sections.title: Any damage to frames
sections.text:
Repair or replace damaged frame members, stops, fixings, joints, and reinforcement so the frame remains sound, square, and capable of supporting the leaf, hinges, closers, locks, and seals. Replace the frame where cracking, splitting, rot, corrosion, distortion, failed stops, loose joints, or failed anchorage affects performance.

Where damage to the frame has also affected the surrounding opening or compartment line, carry out associated builder's works and reinstate the doorset and fire stopping to a compliant standard.

sections.title: Frame loose / failed anchorage
sections.text:
Secure the frame properly to the structure using compatible fixings and reinstate any failed packers, anchors, or reinforcement. The frame must be rigid, square, and capable of supporting the door and all ironmongery without movement.

If the substrate is unsound, the frame has been incorrectly installed, or the opening has moved so that secure fixing cannot be achieved, carry out remedial builder's works and replace or reinstall the doorset.

sections.title: Stops missing / damaged / loose
sections.text:
Repair or replace loose, damaged, incomplete, or missing frame stops so the leaf seats correctly against the frame and seals can perform as intended. Use compatible stop profiles and fixings suitable for the doorset.

Where planted stops have been removed, over-trimmed, or cannot be reinstated compliantly, replace the affected frame component or the complete frame.

sections.title: Gaps between frame and wall / fire stopping around frame
sections.text:
Seal all gaps between the frame and the surrounding wall with appropriate tested fire-stopping materials and reinstate any missing or damaged fire stopping. Remove standard builders' foam, domestic filler, or non-tested packing where it compromises fire resistance.

If the opening, wall, or structural surround is defective, arrange remedial builder's works and then refit or replace the doorset as required.

sections.title: Builder's foam / non-tested filler around frame
sections.text:
Remove non-tested foam, decorator's caulk, expanding filler, mortar snots, or improvised packing from around the frame where these have been used in place of proper fire stopping. Reinstate the perimeter with a tested fire-stopping system compatible with the wall type, frame type, and required fire resistance.

Where hidden voids are suspected, open up as necessary, inspect the full perimeter, and reinstate properly rather than spot-filling visible gaps only.

sections.title: Door certification / evidence of fire rating
sections.text:
Confirm the door's fire-resisting status from a certification label or plug, manufacturer data, project records, or competent survey. Where no reliable evidence exists and the door may not be fire resisting, obtain specialist assessment or replace it with a suitable certificated doorset.

Any new or replacement door should match the required fire and smoke rating for its location and should be installed with compatible tested components.

sections.title: Certification label / plug missing, painted over or unreadable
sections.text:
Where a certification plug, label, or traceable identification mark has been removed, painted over, or is unreadable, clean or expose it only if this can be done without damage. If the door cannot otherwise be verified from records or manufacturer evidence, treat the rating as unconfirmed and seek specialist assessment or replacement.

Do not assume a door is fire resisting simply because it looks substantial or has fire door signs fitted.

sections.title: Door rating not suitable for location / wrong doorset installed
sections.text:
Replace any door or complete doorset that does not provide the fire and smoke performance required for its location, use, and fire strategy. This includes doors of the wrong rating, wrong smoke-control classification, or wrong doorset type for the wall construction or escape function.

Where doubt exists, verify the required performance from the fire strategy, fire risk assessment, design records, or competent fire door survey before specifying replacement.

sections.title: Incompatible replacement leaf in existing frame
sections.text:
Where a replacement leaf has been fitted into an existing frame without evidence that the leaf, frame, seals, glazing, and ironmongery are compatible as a tested assembly, obtain supporting evidence or replace the arrangement with a suitable certificated doorset. Adjustments alone must not be used to legitimise an incompatible pairing.

If the mixed assembly cannot be proven, the safest remedy is replacement of the full doorset.

sections.title: Door construction / thickness
sections.text:
Where the leaf is hollow core, excessively thin, heavily altered, heavily panelled without evidence, or otherwise clearly inconsistent with a fire-resisting doorset, replace it with a suitable certificated fire door or doorset. Older notional doors should only be retained where a competent assessment and the fire risk assessment confirm they remain fit for purpose in that location.

Do not attempt to upgrade obviously unsuitable non-fire-resisting doors by adding seals, plates, or closers alone.

sections.title: Composite / UPVC / non-tested replacement door in a fire-resisting location
sections.text:
Replace any composite, UPVC, domestic security, or other non-tested replacement door that has been installed in a location requiring a fire-resisting doorset unless there is clear evidence that the full assembly is suitable for that purpose. This is particularly relevant to flat entrance doors, communal doors, riser doors, and doors protecting escape routes.

The replacement should include a compatible frame, seals, glazing, ironmongery, threshold detail, and self-closing device as required by the location.

sections.title: Number of hinges (If only 2 hinges on riser door)
sections.text:
Install the missing hinge or hinges so the door has the quantity required by its test evidence. In most cases this will be a minimum of 3 certified fire-rated hinges, with 4 where the door is particularly large, heavy, or intensively used.

Any 2-hinge arrangement on a very small riser door (under 1200mm) should only be retained where the manufacturer or test evidence specifically permits it. Reposition hinges if current fixing locations do not match the approved detail.

sections.title: Are all hinges fire rated
sections.text:
Replace all non-fire-rated, damaged, worn, or unsuitable hinges with certified fire-rated hinges compatible with the door weight, door rating, and doorset evidence. Do not mix incompatible hinge types on the same door unless this is specifically permitted.

Fit the correct screws and any required pads, liners, or packers in accordance with the product data or test evidence.

sections.title: Hinge condition / missing or broken screws
sections.text:
Tighten loose hinges and replace missing, loose, corroded, or broken screws with the correct fire-rated fixings. Repair stripped fixing points only where this can be done without weakening the leaf or frame and is consistent with the doorset evidence.

If the hinge knuckles, leaves, frame, or leaf edge are damaged beyond repair, replace the affected components or the complete doorset.

sections.title: Hinge pads / liners / intumescent pads missing or incorrect
sections.text:
Fit the required hinge pads, liners, packers, or other associated components where these form part of the tested hinge detail. Remove non-approved shims, improvised spacers, or unsuitable packers that alter the geometry or performance of the hinge installation.

Where the hinge recesses have been over-cut or damaged, repair them only where there is suitable evidence; otherwise replace the affected component.

sections.title: Intumescent strips
sections.text:
Replace missing, damaged, loose, discontinuous, incorrectly sized, or incorrectly located intumescent strips with compatible products in the correct position and profile for the doorset. Reinstate the correct groove detail or carrier arrangement where previous alteration has removed the seals.

Where the seal channel, edge detail, or leaf condition cannot be restored properly, replace the door leaf, frame component, or complete doorset.

sections.title: Smoke seals / cold smoke seals
sections.text:
Replace missing, damaged, flattened, torn, detached, or ineffective smoke seals so they make correct contact with the leaf or frame and provide the required smoke control for that location. Ensure any replacement seal is compatible with the doorset and its smoke-control requirement.

Where smoke leakage persists because of poor door geometry, excessive gaps, or incompatible threshold details, correct those defects or replace the leaf or doorset rather than adding improvised brushes or domestic seals.

sections.title: Incorrect seal type / size / location
sections.text:
Remove seals that are the wrong profile, size, material, or location for the doorset and replace them with compatible tested products. This includes using the correct combined or separate intumescent and smoke seals for the required fire and smoke performance.

Do not substitute acoustic, weather, or domestic draught seals for fire and smoke seals unless there is evidence that the product is suitable for the doorset.

sections.title: Seals loose / cut short / discontinuous
sections.text:
Refit or replace seals that have shrunk back, been cut short, pulled away, been mitred badly, or are otherwise non-continuous. Ensure corners, meeting edges, and transitions are complete and installed in the correct orientation.

If the carriers, grooves, or edge details are damaged so the seals cannot be retained securely, repair the detail where permitted or replace the affected component.

sections.title: Are seals painted over
sections.text:
Remove paint contamination only if this can be done without damaging the seals. Where painted-over seals have hardened, detached, lost flexibility, or lost performance, replace the affected smoke seals and intumescent strips.

Record the issue as a maintenance defect and reinforce decorating controls so future painting does not impair fire door components.

sections.title: Threshold seal / automatic drop seal missing or defective
sections.text:
Install, adjust, repair, or replace any threshold seal or automatic drop seal required for smoke control where it is missing, damaged, loose, jammed, worn out, or not dropping fully. Check the operating plunger, housing, fixing points, and contact pressure to ensure the seal deploys correctly without dragging.

Where the threshold detail cannot be made compliant within the doorset evidence, replace the relevant component or complete doorset rather than fitting untested aftermarket products.

sections.title: Does the door close fully
sections.text:
Adjust or replace the self-closing device so the door closes fully into the frame from any angle and overcomes latch resistance. Rectify floor friction, hinge wear, frame distortion, warped leaves, pressure imbalance, or misaligned latch keeps that prevent full closure.

Remove wedges, disconnected closer arms, or any other condition that prevents the door from self-closing. Replace the leaf or doorset if reliable self-closing cannot be restored.

sections.title: Self-closing device missing
sections.text:
Install a suitable compatible self-closing device where one is required but has been removed, omitted, or never fitted. The closer should match the door size, weight, rating, usage pattern, and location, and should be fitted in accordance with the doorset evidence.

Where the fire strategy allows omission of a self-closer for a particular locked-shut service door, record the basis clearly and ensure the locking regime remains effective.

sections.title: Self-closing device damaged / leaking / disconnected
sections.text:
Replace or repair damaged, oil-leaking, seized, disconnected, bent, vandalised, or otherwise defective self-closing devices and their brackets, arms, shoes, or covers. Reinstate all fixings properly and repair damaged fixing points before recommissioning the door.

Do not leave a fire door in use with a disconnected closer arm, leaking closer body, or improvised repairs.

sections.title: Closer power / speed / latching action incorrect
sections.text:
Adjust or replace the closer so the closing speed, sweep, backcheck, and latching action are appropriate for the door and do not cause slamming, rebound, incomplete closure, or failure to latch. The door must close reliably from all normal opening angles while remaining safe in everyday use.

If the required performance cannot be achieved because the closer is undersized, oversized, incompatible, or incorrectly positioned, replace it with a suitable approved unit.

sections.title: Concealed closer / floor spring / pivot closer defective
sections.text:
Repair or replace defective concealed closers, floor springs, pivots, transom closers, or associated hardware so the door closes, aligns, and latches correctly. Check for wear, oil leakage, loose top pivots, damaged boxes, and failed fixings.

Where concealed hardware defects have damaged the leaf, frame, or floor box and cannot be corrected reliably, replace the affected assembly or complete doorset.

sections.title: Door retained open / wedged open
sections.text:
Remove wedges, hooks, kick-down retainers, straps, tied-back closers, or any other unauthorised method of holding the door open. Fire doors must not be left open unless an approved automatic hold-open or free-swing system is provided and is suitable for the fire strategy.

Where the door needs to be held open for operational reasons, provide an approved automatic device linked to the relevant fire detection or alarm system, or change the operation of the space.

sections.title: Hold-open / free-swing / acoustic release device
sections.text:
Repair, replace, or remove damaged, missing, non-approved, or non-functioning hold-open, free-swing, acoustic, or electromagnetic release devices. Test that any retained-open fire door releases correctly under local test and on relevant alarm operation, and that the door then closes and latches properly.

If the fire strategy does not justify a hold-open function, remove the device and restore normal compliant self-closing operation.

Inspect hold-open doors which are fitted with self-closing devices for potential warping / twisting due to the counteracting forces acting on the door.

sections.title: Opening restricted by floor covering / door stop / pressure imbalance / obstruction
sections.text:
Remove or alter any floor finish, threshold strip, mat, furniture, door stop, overhead restrictor, plant item, or environmental condition that prevents the door from opening or closing correctly. Where air pressure, smoke control plant, or ventilation imbalance prevents reliable closure, arrange mechanical and fire strategy review and then recommission the door.

Do not simply increase closer force to mask an underlying obstruction or pressure problem if that creates unsafe use or damages the doorset.

sections.title: Does the door latch positively
sections.text:
Adjust the latch, keep, strike plate, and overall geometry so the door closes firmly onto the latch without manual assistance and without slamming. Replace worn or incompatible latches or locks with compatible fire-rated ironmongery where required.

If the latch cannot engage because of warping, misalignment, or frame distortion, correct the geometry first and then recommission the self-closing action.

sections.title: Lock / latch / keep / strike misalignment
sections.text:
Realign or replace the latch case, keep, strike, faceplate, forend, or associated fixings where poor alignment prevents smooth operation, positive latching, or correct closing pressure. Repair damaged mortices and fixing points only where this can be done without compromising fire performance.

If the lock area has been enlarged excessively, split, or weakened, replace the affected component or the leaf.

sections.title: Lock / latch / ironmongery not fire rated or incompatible
sections.text:
Replace non-fire-rated, non-compatible, damaged, or unsuitable locks, latches, cylinders, handles, escutcheons, and other ironmongery with components appropriate to the required rating and use of the doorset. Verify that the replacement hardware is suitable for timber or steel doors as applicable.

Do not install domestic security hardware, non-rated mortice latches, or unverified aftermarket ironmongery on a fire door.

sections.title: Lock case / closer / ironmongery intumescent protection missing where required
sections.text:
Fit any required intumescent kits, wraps, pads, gaskets, or liners associated with locks, latches, closers, flush bolts, letterplates, viewers, or other ironmongery where the tested detail requires them. Reinstate the correct arrangement after any hardware replacement.

If the original tested detail cannot be established, seek manufacturer guidance or competent specialist advice before reworking the preparation.

sections.title: Handles / lever furniture loose or damaged
sections.text:
Tighten, repair, or replace loose, damaged, worn, or incompatible handles, levers, roses, backplates, spindles, springs, and fixings so the hardware operates smoothly and returns correctly. Ensure the furniture does not foul the frame, stop, seal, or signage and does not prevent the latch from operating.

Where enlarged fixing holes or broken fixings have weakened the leaf, repair or replace the affected area or the leaf as appropriate.

sections.title: Locking arrangements for riser / plant / service cupboard doors
sections.text:
Reinstate the correct locking and closing arrangement where doors are required to be kept locked shut, such as riser, plant, service, meter, and intake cupboard doors. Ensure the door is secure, in good condition, and fitted with the correct signage where required.

Replace non-compliant locks, latches, closers, or strike arrangements with compatible fire-rated components. Where the fire strategy allows omission of a self-closer because the door is kept locked shut, make sure the locking regime is robust and documented.

sections.title: Escape-route opening hardware
sections.text:
For doors on escape routes, replace locks, fastenings, thumb-turns, access-control arrangements, or other hardware that prevents immediate opening from the escape side. Reconfigure the door so it opens quickly and safely in fire conditions while maintaining the required fire resistance and self-closing performance.

Where the risk assessment or occupancy requires panic or emergency exit hardware, install the correct compatible device rather than relying on domestic locks or multiple actions.

sections.title: Access control / maglock / electric strike / emergency release issues
sections.text:
Reconfigure or replace access control, electromagnetic locks, electric strikes, emergency release units, power supplies, or interfaces that compromise safe escape, door closing, or fail-safe operation in fire conditions. Ensure the arrangement releases or permits safe use as required by the escape strategy and does not hold the door in a dangerous condition on fire alarm, power failure, or fault.

Any electrical work should be coordinated with the fire alarm, security, and access-control systems and then fully retested.

sections.title: Panic bar / push pad / emergency exit device defective
sections.text:
Repair or replace damaged, stiff, loose, incomplete, or non-compliant panic bars, push pads, latches, and associated fixings so the door opens immediately and safely in the direction of escape. Ensure the device is compatible with the fire door, occupancy profile, and required operating mode.

Where the device has damaged the leaf or frame or has been fitted to an unsuitable door, carry out associated repairs or replace the doorset.

sections.title: Security chain / night latch / additional surface bolts / secondary security devices
sections.text:
Remove non-approved security chains, additional bolts, hasps, padlocks, bars, door guards, or other secondary security devices that compromise fire performance, self-closing, or emergency escape. Replace them with a compliant locking solution where additional security is genuinely required.

If previous installations have left holes or weakened the leaf or frame, repair those areas where permitted or replace the affected component.

sections.title: Fire door keep shut / keep locked signs
sections.text:
Fit the correct fire door signage where the fire strategy, site standard, or legal duty requires it. In common parts, self-closing fire doors will normally need 'Fire door keep shut' signs, while doors that must be kept locked shut should display the appropriate 'Fire door keep locked shut' signage in the correct position.

Do not add signage in a way that compromises the leaf. If signage is not required for that door type or location, record the basis for omission in the fire risk assessment or inspection standard.

sections.title: Signage damaged / wrong wording / obscured / incorrectly placed
sections.text:
Replace damaged, missing, painted-over, obscured, badly positioned, or incorrect signage with the correct fire door sign for the door's function. Remove duplicate or conflicting signs where they create confusion.

Re-fix signs using a method that does not damage the door leaf, seals, or glazing and does not conflict with the doorset evidence.

sections.title: Glazing / vision panel fire resistance
sections.text:
Replace cracked, loose, incorrectly marked, non-fire-resisting, or damaged glazing with a fully compatible fire-resisting glazing system. Where the glazing type cannot be verified from markings, manufacturer data, or test evidence, obtain specialist advice or replace the glazed assembly.

Do not cut new glazing apertures or alter existing ones unless this is specifically permitted by the doorset evidence and carried out by a competent specialist.

sections.title: Glazing  panel above / to the side of fire doors
sections.text: Glazing panels, including top lights (above) and sidelights (to the side) of fire doors, must be part of a certified, fully tested fire-rated assembly, typically requiring 30 (FD30) or 60 (FD60) minutes of fire resistance. These panels must utilize fire-rated glass and be installed with specific, compatible framing and intumescent materials to prevent smoke and flame spread.

sections.title: Glass marking absent / glazing unverifiable
sections.text:
Where the installed glass cannot be identified from permanent marking, manufacturer data, or project records, treat the glazing as unverified until suitable evidence is obtained. If the assembly cannot be proven, replace the glass and associated system with a fully compatible fire-resisting arrangement.

Do not rely on appearance alone to confirm that glazing is fire resisting.

sections.title: Glazing beads / glazing system
sections.text:
Refix or replace loose, missing, damaged, or non-compliant glazing beads, pins, clips, gaskets, and associated components with tested parts that match the glazing system. Ensure the beads are the correct material, size, orientation, and fixing detail for the fire door.

If the glazing build-up cannot be restored to a compliant tested arrangement, replace the leaf or complete doorset.

sections.title: Glazing gaskets / sealants missing or incompatible
sections.text:
Replace missing, damaged, hardened, wrongly specified, or improvised glazing gaskets, tapes, setting blocks, and sealants with products compatible with the tested glazing detail. Remove domestic mastics, decorators' fillers, or silicone sealants where these have been substituted for the correct system.

Where previous work has contaminated or damaged the glazing aperture beyond simple reinstatement, replace the glazed assembly or the leaf.

sections.title: Glazing aperture altered / oversized / unauthorised cut-out
sections.text:
Where a glazing opening has been enlarged, re-cut, moved, or otherwise altered without supporting evidence, do not attempt ad hoc repair around the aperture. Obtain specialist evidence for an approved repair only if available; otherwise replace the leaf or complete doorset.

The same approach applies where the aperture edge is split, charred, over-routed, or no longer capable of supporting the tested glazing system.

sections.title: Letterbox / letterplate
sections.text:
Repair or replace damaged, jammed-open, non-fire-rated, or poorly installed letterplates and letterboxes with a compatible fire-resisting product. Ensure the flap closes properly and that any replacement unit is installed with the correct liner, protection, and fixings where required by the doorset evidence.

If a letterplate has been added, changed, or enlarged without evidence, verify that the product and aperture are suitable for the door. If the existing cut-out compromises performance and cannot be remediated properly, replace the door leaf.

sections.title: Spyhole / viewer non-fire-rated or unauthorised
sections.text:
Remove and replace non-fire-rated, damaged, loose, oversized, or unauthorised viewers with a compatible fire-rated viewer only where the doorset evidence permits that preparation. If the hole size, position, or installation method cannot be justified or repaired compliantly, replace the door leaf.

Do not drill additional holes for viewers, bells, intercoms, cameras, or similar accessories unless the doorset evidence specifically permits it.

sections.title: Ventilation grille / louvre / transfer grille non-compliant
sections.text:
Remove or replace non-fire-rated, damaged, or unauthorised grilles, louvres, or transfer vents with a compatible tested fire-resisting arrangement only where the doorset evidence allows such an opening. If the opening itself cannot be justified or repaired, replace the door leaf or doorset.

Do not fit domestic ventilation grilles or intumescent products in a way that is not supported by the tested detail for that door.

sections.title: Cat flap / pet door / service hatch added to fire door
sections.text:
Remove unauthorised cat flaps, pet doors, service hatches, access panels, or other cut-outs from fire doors. Unless there is specific tested evidence for an approved repair, replace the affected leaf or complete doorset.

Any associated damage to the frame, seals, or threshold should be rectified as part of the replacement works.

sections.title: Kick plate / finger guard / protection plate non-compliant
sections.text:
Remove, repair, or replace oversized, loose, damaged, combustible, or non-compliant kick plates, push plates, finger guards, edge protectors, and other surface-mounted protection that is not supported by the doorset evidence. Install compatible protective hardware only where it does not compromise the fire or smoke performance of the door.

If previous plates or guards have hidden damage, holes, or over-cut areas, inspect the substrate and repair or replace as necessary.

sections.title: Additional holes / abandoned ironmongery cut-outs / excessive morticing
sections.text:
Repair or replace leaves and frames where previous hardware changes have left open holes, enlarged mortices, abandoned preparations, or excessive routing that weakens the assembly. Small repairs should only be undertaken where the repair method is compatible with the doorset evidence.

Where the leaf or frame has been materially weakened by repeated hardware changes, replacement is usually the appropriate remedy.

sections.title: Temporary repairs / non-tested filler / taped repairs
sections.text:
Remove temporary or improvised repairs such as tape, decorator's filler, expanding foam, non-tested mastic, glued-on patches, plastic trims, or surface-applied timber used to disguise defects. Reinstate the component using a compatible repair method supported by evidence, or replace it.

Do not accept cosmetic make-good works as a substitute for a compliant fire door repair.

sections.title: Unauthorised alterations / non-compliant hardware
sections.text:
Remove or replace non-compliant viewers, grilles, access devices, additional bolts, plates, intercoms, cameras, cable pass-throughs, or other alterations that are not supported by the door certification or test evidence. Reinstate the door to a known compliant configuration.

If the integrity of the leaf or frame has been significantly compromised by unauthorised work, replace the door leaf or complete doorset.

sections.title: Double door meeting stiles / pair alignment
sections.text:
Realign or replace damaged meeting edges, rebated meeting stiles, astragals, and related seals so the door pair closes tightly and the fire and smoke gaps are controlled. Adjust hinges, closers, and frame geometry so both leaves meet correctly without fouling or overlap problems.

If pair alignment cannot be maintained because of frame movement, leaf distortion, or damage to the meeting edges, replace the pair or complete doorset.

sections.title: Door selector / coordinator on double doors
sections.text:
Repair, adjust, or replace the selector or coordinator so double doors close in the correct sequence and the active and passive leaves meet, latch, and seal correctly. Recommission associated closers, meeting-edge seals, and flush bolts after adjustment and retest the full closing sequence.

Where sequence control cannot be restored because of incompatible ironmongery or distorted leaves, replace the affected components or the complete pair.

sections.title: Flush bolts / shoot bolts / inactive leaf securing hardware
sections.text:
Repair or replace damaged, missing, stiff, loose, or misaligned flush bolts, shoot bolts, edge bolts, guides, and keep plates so the inactive leaf secures properly at the head and threshold and releases safely for use. Ensure the hardware is compatible with the fire rating and closing sequence of the door pair.

Where previous bolt preparations have damaged the leaf edges or meeting stile beyond repair, replace the leaf or doorset.

sections.title: Meeting-edge seals / astragal / rebated pair edge defects
sections.text:
Replace damaged, missing, loose, or non-compliant astragals, meeting-edge seals, rebated edge components, and associated fixings so the pair controls smoke and fire spread correctly. Confirm that any replacement arrangement matches the tested detail for the pair of doors.

If the meeting edge has been cut back, split, or altered so that the tested detail cannot be restored, replace the affected leaves or the complete pair.

sections.title: Overpanel / side panel / fanlight associated with the doorset
sections.text:
Repair or replace surrounding solid or glazed panels that form part of the doorset where they are loose, damaged, poorly fixed, or not fire resisting. The whole assembly must perform correctly, not just the door leaf.

Where the surrounding panel construction cannot be verified or restored, replace the complete doorset and associated screens or panels.

sections.title: Flat entrance door replaced with non-fire-resisting door
sections.text:
Replace any non-fire-resisting replacement flat entrance door with a suitable certificated fire door or doorset, including compatible frame, seals, glazing, letterplate, ironmongery, threshold detail, and self-closing device as required for the location. Record access attempts and resident engagement where access to flats is needed to complete the work.

Any associated security upgrade should be achieved through a tested fire-resisting doorset rather than a domestic security door.

sections.title: Flat entrance door closer removed or disabled
sections.text:
Reinstate or replace the self-closing device on any flat entrance door where it has been removed, disconnected, disabled, or allowed to fail. The door should close fully into the frame and latch from any normal opening angle without manual assistance.

Where the removal of the closer has damaged the leaf or frame, repair the preparation where permitted or replace the affected component.

sections.title: Rising butt hinges used as the closer on a flat entrance door
sections.text:
Do not rely on rising butt hinges as the closing method for flat entrance doors. Install a suitable self-closing device that closes the door from any angle against latch resistance and is compatible with the doorset evidence.

After conversion, check the frame, hinges, latch, and overall door geometry and recommission the door so it closes and latches correctly.

sections.title: Doors to ancillary rooms / meter cupboards / risers
sections.text:
Ensure these doors provide the required fire resistance, fit correctly in their frames, and are either effectively self-closing or robustly kept locked shut, depending on the fire strategy. Upgrade or replace non-fire-resisting, damaged, ill-fitting, poorly secured, or poorly signed ancillary room, riser, plant, and meter cupboard doors.

Where service cupboards contain significant ignition sources or services penetrating compartments, coordinate the door works with any required compartmentation and service sealing works.

sections.title: Door swing direction incorrect for escape strategy
sections.text:
Where a door on an escape route opens in the wrong direction for the occupancy, risk profile, or escape strategy, rehang or replace the door and associated hardware so the route can be used safely in an emergency. Any change must preserve the required fire resistance, self-closing function, and security arrangement.

Before altering handing or swing direction, verify the required arrangement from the fire strategy and means-of-escape design.

sections.title: Double action, 2 way swing door
sections.text: Double-action,  2-way swing fire door hinges allow doors to swing in both directions while maintaining fire safety compliance (typically FD30 or FD60). Generally used in high traffic (hospitals/corridor/kitchen doors) these require a minimum of three certified fire-rated, double-action spring hinges or, preferably, floor springs for proper fire integrity. All fire doors must use hinges certified to BS EN 1935, and while three is standard, heavier or taller doors may require four to prevent warping. These hinges, often featuring an enclosed, spring-loaded design for self-closing including intumescent pads to ensure the door seals properly during a fire.

sections.title: Steel doorset corrosion / denting / damaged gaskets
sections.text:
Remove corrosion, replace damaged components, and repair or replace any dented, distorted, perforated, or poorly aligned steel leaf, frame, or hardware reinforcement that affects closing, latching, or fire performance. Replace damaged gaskets and seals with compatible products for the steel doorset.

Where corrosion or distortion is advanced, replacement of the complete steel doorset is usually the appropriate remedy.

sections.title: Paint build-up / decorative damage affecting operation
sections.text:
Remove excessive paint build-up from hinges, seals, latches, closers, thresholds, and meeting edges where it is preventing normal operation. Replace components that have been damaged by painting, decorating, or surface preparation, including painted-over seals, blocked hinges, and glued-up latches.

Implement decorating controls so future works do not impair seals, labels, signage, ironmongery, or door clearances.

sections.title: Non-Painted surfaces of fire door leaf / frame
sections.text: Fire doors can be painted to improve appearance or match decor, but they do not need to be painted for functionality, as they are generally finished upon installation. Use water-based paint (fire-rated paint is recommended) for the best finish and safety, thick oil-based paint can hinder performance. Prepare the door by sanding, cleaning with sugar soap, and applying a primer before top-coating, though. Key restrictions include never painting over hinges, hardware, or seals

sections.title: Services / access control cabling / penetrations through leaf or frame
sections.text:
Remove or properly rework non-compliant cables, conduits, readers, contact switches, power transfers, intercoms, and other service penetrations that have compromised the leaf, frame, or fire stopping. Reinstate the door or frame using a tested detail where one exists, or replace the affected component.

Coordinate remedial works with access-control and fire alarm contractors so the final arrangement is both functional and fire compliant.

sections.title: Floor threshold / saddle / plate defective or incompatible
sections.text:
Repair, replace, or remove damaged, loose, raised, or incompatible thresholds, saddles, weather bars, threshold plates, and transition strips that interfere with self-closing, threshold sealing, or safe passage. Ensure any new threshold detail is compatible with the fire door, accessibility needs, and smoke-control requirement.

Where a threshold component forms part of a tested smoke-control arrangement, replace it with the correct compatible product rather than a generic trim or strip.

sections.title: Resident or contractor alterations to flat entrance doors
sections.text:
Reinstate any flat entrance door altered by residents or contractors without approval, including changed hardware, drilled holes, replaced letterplates, viewers, additional locks, decorative coverings, or removed closers and seals. Obtain proof of suitability for any component that is proposed to remain.

If the alterations cannot be justified by test evidence and competent installation, replace the leaf or complete doorset and restore a compliant flat entrance door arrangement.

sections.title: Overhead stop / door check / restrictor interfering with fire door performance
sections.text:
Adjust, relocate, repair, or remove any overhead stop, door check, restrictor, closer stay, wall stop, or floor stop that prevents the door from closing correctly, damages the closer, or causes pull-out at fixings. Ensure the final arrangement protects the wall and hardware without impairing fire performance.

Where repeated over-opening has damaged the frame, leaf, or closer fixing positions, repair or replace those components as part of the remedial works.

sections.title: Frame or wall opening movement / cracking affecting doorset
sections.text:
Where cracking, settlement, structural movement, or distortion of the wall opening has affected the frame geometry, arrange investigation and builder's works before attempting final adjustment of the doorset. Once the opening is stable, reset or replace the frame, reinstate fire stopping, and recommission the door.

Repeated readjustment of hardware alone will not correct an unstable opening.
